Tactical.MovementHint: Movement points per hex. Turning costs one point per hex-side during a move, and is free at the end of one — to any facing if you spent no more than half your points, otherwise by a single hex-side.
Tactical.Immobile: This posture cannot move hex by hex: sitting cannot move at all, and lying down spends every movement point to shift one hex.

Rules.Title: GURPS rules in play
Rules.MenuHint: Turn individual GURPS rules on or off for this world. A rule that is off behaves as though it had never been written — no penalty, no control, nothing to explain.
Rules.Intro: GURPS is written to be played at several depths. Everything here is optional detail; the spine — success rolls, damage, DR and the active defenses — is always in play.

feint.Name: Feint
feint.Hint: Fake an attack: a Quick Contest of weapon skills whose margin comes off the foe's next defense.

deceptiveAttack.Name: Deceptive Attack
deceptiveAttack.Hint: Trade two points of your own skill for one off the foe's defenses.

rapidStrike.Name: Rapid Strike
rapidStrike.Hint: A second attack in the time of one, both at -6.

retreat.Name: Retreating
retreat.Hint: Step back as you defend: +3 to Dodge, +1 to most parries and blocks.

rapidFire.Name: Rapid fire
rapidFire.Hint: Fire a burst: a bonus for the shots sent, and Recoil decides how many land.

opportunityFire.Name: Opportunity fire
opportunityFire.Hint: Cover ground with a ready weapon on a Wait, and pay for how much of it.

closeCombat.Name: Close combat
closeCombat.Hint: Sharing a hex: only a weapon that reaches close is any use there.

slams.Name: Slams
slams.Hint: Run into someone. Damage comes off how fast you were going.

evading.Name: Evading
evading.Hint: Get past someone without knocking them down, as a Quick Contest of DX.

hitLocations.Name: Hit locations
hitLocations.Hint: Aim at a part of the body, with its own to-hit penalty, DR and wounding.

knockback.Name: Knockback
knockback.Hint: A heavy blow throws the target back, and may knock them down.

criticalTables.Name: Critical hit and miss tables
criticalTables.Hint: A critical does something in particular rather than only being named.

explosions.Name: Explosions
explosions.Hint: Collateral damage falling off with distance, and fragmentation.

afflictions.Name: Afflictions
afflictions.Hint: Attacks resisted with an attribute roll rather than doing damage.

regularContests.Name: Regular Contests
regularContests.Hint: A drawn-out contest of repeated rolls, rather than one apiece.

frightChecks.Name: Fright Checks
frightChecks.Hint: A Will roll against horror, with the Fright Check Table for failures.

extraEffort.Name: Extra Effort
extraEffort.Hint: Spend fatigue to push a roll or a feat of strength beyond its usual limit.

physicalActivities.Name: Physical activities
physicalActivities.Hint: Climbing, jumping, swimming, running, throwing distance and lifting.

CombatStyle.Name: Combat system
CombatStyle.Hint: Basic combat is abstract: everyone can reach everyone and nobody has a back. Tactical combat is fought on a hex map, where facing decides what you can defend against. Tactical needs a hex-gridded scene; on any other grid the table falls back to basic.

Hint.points: How many points the character is built on, and how many may come back from disadvantages. Both are the GM's call for the campaign.
Hint.attributes: ST, DX, IQ and HT start at 10. Everything else on the sheet is worked out from them.
Hint.advantages: What the character is unusually good at. The cost comes off the budget above.
Hint.disadvantages: What the character is stuck with. These pay points back, up to the limit above.
Hint.skills: What the character has learned. Points spent on each are set on the sheet afterwards.
Hint.gear: What the character carries. Weight counts against encumbrance once it is marked carried.
Hint.review: What the character has come to. Nothing here is fixed — the sheet edits all of it.

Skill.SpendMore: Spend the next step of points
Skill.SpendLess: Take back the last step of points

Trait.CostTableHint: A few traits are priced from a table rather than at a flat rate per level: Wealth runs 10/20/30/50/75. Fill this in and it replaces the points and per-level figures. Leave it empty for the great majority, which are priced evenly.

Item.Name: Item name
Item.NoModesYet: No attacks yet. Add one to make this a weapon.

Hint.DisadvantageLimit: A rule of thumb, not a hard cap. Disadvantages and quirks both count.
Hint.Languages: Accented is -1 to skills that depend on language. One native language is free.
Hint.NoMeleeAttacks: No melee attacks. Add equipment with an attack mode on the Gear tab.
Hint.Overloaded: Carrying more than ten times Basic Lift. This character cannot move under this load.
Hint.Techniques: bought up from a prerequisite skill
Hint.HitLocations: Unaimed blows hit the torso. Eye and Vitals can only be targeted deliberately, and only by impaling, piercing or tight-beam burning attacks.

Roll.TooLowToAttempt: {label}: effective {effective} is below 3, so the roll cannot be attempted.

Chat.Blast: Explosion — collateral damage out to {yards} yards
Chat.NoTarget: Target or select a token first.
Chat.CannotApply: You do not have permission to change: {names}
Chat.MajorWound: Major wound — HT roll to avoid knockdown and stunning
Chat.ConsciousnessRoll: HT roll to stay conscious, at
Chat.SubtractDR: Subtract the target's DR from basic damage, then apply the wounding modifier.
Chat.SubtractDRDivisor: Divide the target's DR by {divisor} (rounding down), subtract it from basic damage, then apply the wounding modifier.

Technique.MaxRelativeHint: Relative to the prerequisite skill. Zero lets the technique reach that skill but not exceed it.

Armor.LocationsHint: Locations covered. Leave all unticked for whole-body coverage.
Armor.SplitHint: Armour written “4/2” stops one kind of attack better than another. Leave the second DR blank unless it does.
